name: factory
description: A software factory: an intake on opus weighs each feature or GitHub issue labeled factory, reviewers are routed by risk, up to three runs work at once. /factory <feature> writes a spec, has you approve its plan (in goal-run when it's installed), builds it on a branch, runs the checks and parallel reviews, and has an approver agent decide; you then press Open PR and Claude opens it. Its pane draws where the run is

checks.title: Check commands
checks.description: Commands the factory runs after each build, separated by ; (no shell), e.g. npm test; npm run lint. Empty uses .factory/checks.json, else detects them (node, python, go, cargo, make, maven/gradle, dotnet; root, one level down, touched folders) plus allowlisted commands in the spec acceptance criteria

maxRounds.title: Review rounds
maxRounds.description: How many times reviewers may send the builder back before the approver decides

setup.title: Setup command
setup.description: Commands that install the dependencies in a run's fresh worktree before its first checks, separated by ; (no shell), e.g. npm ci. Empty uses the lockfile (npm ci, pnpm or yarn install) when node_modules is missing

autoPr.title: Open the PR without asking
autoPr.description: on: the PR is opened as soon as the approver agent approves. off: the run waits for you to press Open PR

skeptic.title: Skeptic before a fix round
skeptic.description: on: before the builder is sent back over blocker and major findings, a read-only skeptic tries to refute each with evidence; refuted findings are dropped (and named to the approver), so no round is spent on a finding that isn't real. A security blocker always stands

checkTimeout.title: Check time limit (minutes)
checkTimeout.description: How long one check may run before it counts as timed out: the run then stops for you instead of sending the builder to fix it. Claude Code allows a command 10 minutes at most

baseFailures.title: A check that fails before the change too
baseFailures.description: When a check fails, the factory runs it once on the run's base commit. If it fails there too, the change didn't cause it, and the builder isn't sent after it. go-on: the run goes on to the reviewers, who are told the check fails on the base. stop: the run stops for you

notChecked.title: What the reviewers didn't check
notChecked.description: Each reviewer ends with what it did not verify. record: kept as a line each in .factory/not-checked.jsonl, counted in the status. issue: also opened as one GitHub issue per run, labeled factory-followup (which the factory's queue doesn't take up on its own)

models.title: Models by feature size
models.description: auto: the spec-writer judges the feature small, medium or large, and a large one runs the builder on opus (sonnet otherwise). fixed: sonnet for the spec-writer, builder and code reviewer, opus for the security reviewer and approver, whatever the size

intake.title: Intake and risk routing
intake.description: on: an intake agent (opus) first decides whether the feature is worth building, at what scope, its risk (low, medium, high) and surfaces (ui, security); NEEDS-INFO and REJECT stop for you. Its route then picks the reviewers: code on haiku at low risk, sonnet otherwise (opus when the diff calls for depth); security (opus) only for a security surface, high risk or a sensitive diff; ux (sonnet) and ui-design (haiku) for a UI surface or UI files. Spec-writer, builder and approver run on opus. off: no intake; security and code always review, models by the models option

autoMerge.title: Merge the PR on APPROVE
autoMerge.description: on: once the approver agent approves and the checks pass again on the latest base, Claude merges the PR as soon as it opens it (over GitHub's REST API: gh api -X PUT repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/<number>/merge; branch protection and required checks still apply). An escalation you approve is never merged automatically. off: the PR waits for you to merge it

concurrency.title: Runs at once
concurrency.description: How many runs may work at once, each in its own worktree and branch: /factory run starts that many issues, and a feature you start takes a free slot. A run that waits on you (a plan, a PR, an escalation) holds no slot

skills.title: Skills per role
skills.description: Skills a role loads before its job, in place of the factory's own (factory:spec-writer, factory:builder, factory:security-reviewer, factory:code-reviewer, factory:approver), as role=skill,skill; role=skill (roles: spec, builder, security, code, approver); role=none loads none. E.g. spec=spec-pack; security=security. Empty: every role loads the factory's own skill
